dedupe_keys.name: owbeii gridded emissions from open municipal waste burning in india 0 1 degree 2015

description: This emission inventory estimates the air pollutants released by open burning of municipal waste across India. It was deposited on Mendeley Data by Baerbel Sinha in 2023 and accompanies the paper by Gaurav Sharma, Baerbel Sinha and colleagues in Environmental Science and Technology (2019). Emissions are given in tonnes per year on a 0.1 by 0.1 degree grid for 2015, for carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxide, ammonia, methane, fine and coarse particles, black and organic carbon and many individual volatile organic compounds, with hydrogen chloride in a separate file; coordinates refer to the lower left corner of each cell. A further file gives the amount of waste burned, so users can apply their own emission factors, and the description mentions an updated 2020 inventory with landfill fires. The files are free to download online under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: burning amounts are modelled from waste generation and collection assumptions, and a single year is given. Simulation uses: pollution burden from uncollected waste for waste service gap and health impact models in India. Related records: the EDGAR food system emissions (data-edgar-food) and the EDF landfill methane map (data-edf-landfill-methane-map) cover other waste-related emissions.
